items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Lawrence Brown, Tizol, he'd leave it blank... Puerto Ricans, Tizol, an old Puerto Rican. Yeah, we had everybody.

ctx.x: So Duke wrote your parts out for you.

No. He had what we call a skeleton, had a skeleton, you know, for my part. Just a skeleton. But he let me use my own imagination. He never wrote a part for me. He'd give me a skeleton, and I would rehearse it and I would insert my ideas, like individual solos for the different guys in the band, he never wrote them out.

That's why today those guys are laying in his grave -- they haven't caught us in 25 to 30 years, because it ain't down. Just the basis, and when it comes to a solo and ensembles he wrote those, or have an arranger do it for him, but he knew what he wanted, but like he'd tell Johnny, Tricky, or any of the guys, Lawrence Brown, Tizol, he'd leave it blank. The only thing he'd write, how many choruses he wanted them to play. That's why Johnny Hodges, Carney, there's no more Johnny Hodges, there's no more Harry…
